title: At the Edge of Putnam's Program: Limitative Results For Computable Inductive Logics
summary: The task of inductive logic is to develop a formal framework to analyze inductive reasoning. Historically this was accomplished by assigning probabilities to sentences of a logical language. Two natural criteria for such a system are: (i) the underlying language should be rich enough to express scientific hypotheses, and (ii) the probabilities should be, in some sense, accessible. The first criterion suggests that the language should at least contain the language of arithmetic, while the second suggests that probabilities should be computable. We show that these two criteria are in tension…
